{{Short description|Mathematical group}}
{{for|the finite simple group|Higman–Sims group}}
In [[mathematics]], the '''Higman group''', introduced by {{harvs|txt|first=Graham|last=Higman|authorlink=Graham Higman|year=1951}}, was the first example of an [[infinite group|infinite]] [[finitely presented group|finitely presented]] [[group (mathematics)|group]] with no [[trivial group|nontrivial]] [[finite group|finite]] [[quotient group|quotients]]. 
The quotient by the maximal proper [[normal subgroup]] is a [[finitely generated group|finitely generated]] infinite [[simple group]]. {{harvtxt|Higman|1974}} later found some finitely presented infinite  groups {{math|''G''{{sub|''n'',''r''}}}} that are simple if {{math|''n''}} is even and have a simple [[subgroup]] of [[index of a subgroup|index]] 2 if {{math|''n''}} is odd, one of which is one of the [[Thompson groups]].

Higman's group is generated by 4 elements {{math|''a'', ''b'', ''c'', ''d''}} with the relations
:<math>a^{-1}ba = b^2,\quad b^{-1}cb = c^2,\quad c^{-1}dc = d^2,\quad d^{-1}ad = a^2.</math>
